alice: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change rolled last night I'm seeing a clear regression for small/short requests. p99 for <=12 token requests jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms on hosted canary. Heap/profile points at host-side tokenization + gRPC small-write churn + autobatch fallback. Anyone else?

chris: Can you paste the numbers and a short trace? Also which canary region, SDK vs raw HTTP?

alice: Canary eu-west-1, SDK (node) and raw curl both show it. Quick numbers from synthetic runner against canary:
```
baseline (older runtime): p50=28ms p95=95ms p99=180ms
current (post-change): p50=35ms p95=180ms p99=420ms
CPU per-short-req (host) up ~2.4x, syscalls/writes per response went from ~2 -> ~6
```
Trace snippet (top stack frames):
- runtime::host_tokenizer::bpe_encode
- grpc::slice_write_loop
- host::request_parse::parse_payload
- batcher::autobatch::fallback_send_single

hannah: I reproduced on local dev cluster. Flamegraph shows two hotspots: 1) utf8->bpe path (memcpy heavy) and 2) grpc small-chunk writer loop where each token chunk causes a syscall. Also we see frequent kvcache lookups that appear to thrash for short bursts — likely prefetch logic overfetching for small requests.

ben: Correlating kvcache logs: for short requests we get repeated shard evictions because prefetch window is tuned for median longer sequences. Example logs: 
`kvcache: prefetch(128) -> evict shard-7 (age 3s)`
That eviction rate lines up with latency spikes (lock contention + memcpy churn).

alice: Proposed quick-mitigation options (canary-friendly):
1) header-based token bypass: accept `X-Tokenized: true` with body as newline-separated token ids or protobuf repeated ints -> skip utf8->bpe entirely for internal SDKs. Minimal surface area + opt-in.
2) zero-copy gRPC coalescer: coalesce small slices into one iovec and issue single writev instead of multiple write calls. Behind flag `host.enable_zero_copy_coalesce`. Reduces syscalls dramatically.
3) change autobatch heuristic: currently time-based fallback sends single requests through the old path. Switch to tokens-based heuristic: if tokens <= 16 then route to fast-path (bypass batching state machine), else go through normal batcher.
4) tighten kvcache prefetch for short requests: cap prefetch window to <=4 for tokens<=32 and add per-shard pin for hot small-shard workloads.

chris: Nice. Any numbers on (2)?

hannah: I prototyped coalescer; local tests: syscalls per response 6 -> 1, p99 for small requests improved from 420ms -> 270ms (so not fully back to baseline but big win). Memory overhead nominal; need to watch large-stream responses to avoid amplification. Patch is ~120 lines and toggled behind flag.

ben: For kvcache: simple pinning for small-shard windows reduced eviction rate by ~60% in my run and CPU contention dropped. But it increases tail memory for those nodes; likely ok with per-tenant caps.

chris: Risks? Security/compatibility?

alice: Token-bypass is internal-only (SDK sets header+signed). We should require SDK to sign a small HMAC header so external users can't injest arbitrary token ids. Also fallback validator in runtime to sanity-check token id ranges.

hannah: Zero-copy coalescer interacts with HTTP/gRPC flow control; need to ensure we don't starve other streams on the same connection. P0 test: run with 500 concurrent flows. So we gate it behind canary and per-connection bytes cap.

chris: Plan for rollout:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable zero-copy coalescer behind flag + token-bypass for internal SDK only in eu-west-1 canary (48h)
- Stage 2: enable tokens-based fast-path in batcher (canary -> 10% -> 50%)
- Stage 3: kvcache pin tuning (gradual)
- Stage 4: full prod if no regressions

ben: I'll file PRs: kvcache pin config + telemetry (delta eviction rate metric).
hannah: I'll open coalescer PR behind flag + perf tests (ab, wrk2, flamegraphs).
alice: I'll add SDK header support + HMAC validation + test vectors. I'll also create a synthetic runner job to continuously hammer short-request profile.

perf-bot: Created ticket INF-2379 \"short-request host overhead regression\" and linked PRs: #5483 #5484 #5485.

chris: Great. Assigning owners: alice -> SDK token header, hannah -> coalescer, ben -> kvcache. I'll own rollout and monitoring (dash with p50/p95/p99 + syscall metric).

alice: Sounds good. Quick TODOs in thread:
- alice: SDK change + signed header (target: tomorrow EOD)
- hannah: coalescer PR + perf run (target: 48h)
- ben: kvcache pin PR + telemetry (target: 72h)
- chris: canary toggle + dashboard update (target: 24h)

chris: :thumbsup: If anyone hits blockers ping me in thread. We'll avoid broad rollback unless absolutely necessary.
